crit: Artificial data: 'we decided to prepare artificial data sets in order to control these factors' (noisy and borderline examples, decomposition into sub-clusters/small disjuncts, linear vs non-linear boundaries); the final group (800 examples, IR 1:7, 5 sub-regions) was selected from a preliminary experiment because 'All these sets presented a significant challenge for a stand-alone classifier'. Real data: 'imbalanced data sets that we had used in our previous study [9]', from UCI or the authors' medical case studies (acl).
benchmark_inherited_from: [9] Stefanowski, J., Wilk, S.: Selective pre-processing of imbalanced data for improving classification performance. DaWaK 2008, LNCS 5182, pp. 283-292 (real-life data sets only)
notes: Main study on artificial 2-D data generated by the authors (subclus, clover, paw shapes; 800 examples, IR 1:7; borderline disturbance 0-70%; added C-type noisy minority examples in Sec. 3.3). Real-life part: nine data sets (Table 4: Acl, Breast can., Bupa, Cleveland, Ecoli, Haberman, Hepatitis, New thyr., Pima) reused from the authors' previous study [9]; acl is from the authors' medical case studies (coded Private). The paper prints NO characteristics for any real data set and does not say how data sets such as Ecoli, New thyr. or Cleveland were made two-class or which class is the minority (no binarisation described, so Binarised not coded; Natural coded since data are said to come from UCI/case studies with no modification described). minority_rule coded for the generated data (minority = designed shape); for the real data it is not stated. No data/code release statement. 'NRC' typo for NCR (p.164). Datasets CSV: artificial rows take 800 and 1:7 from text (Sec. 3.1/3.3); feature and class counts are given in words ('two-dimensional space', 'binary'); minority count is not printed.
